result.summary: This PR extends ArgsManager's command-line parser to accept options (like -rpcwallet or -wallet) after the command and its positional arguments, GNU/getopt-long style, instead of silently treating everything after the first non-option argument as positional. Unrecognized options after the command now produce an explicit error instead of being silently absorbed, and a '--' separator lets users pass dash-prefixed positional arguments explicitly. bitcoin-cli's CommandLineRPC and bitcoin-tx's CommandLineRawTx are updated to read from the new parsed command args rather than re-scanning argv, and bitcoin-wallet benefits automatically. Extracted as a focused subset of the larger closed PR #33540.
result.problem: Users of bitcoind's tools (bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-tx, bitcoin-wallet) who place an option after a command or subcommand had that option silently dropped and treated as a positional argument, which could cause an RPC call to hit the wrong wallet or a tool to reject valid input with a confusing error, as shown in the PR's before/after examples.

open_concerns: vicjuma questioned whether the inconsistency between bitcoin-cli (which benefits from GetCommand()) and other tools like bitcoin-tx (which did not, at the time) should be addressed more broadly; author said this PR is intentionally scoped narrower with follow-ups planned, and vicjuma did not push back further.
resolved_concerns: w0xlt: '--' only ended option processing after the command, not before it (e.g. 'bitcoin-wallet -help -- create' failed) — fixed in the final push.
w0xlt: on Windows, a post-command option with a path value like /datadir=C:/bitcoin was mistaken for a positional path — fixed by checking only the option name for embedded slashes.
w0xlt: a lone '-' after a command (e.g. 'bitcoin-cli echo -') was misidentified as an option — fixed by requiring length > 1.
w0xlt: bitcoin-tx broke on a trailing option like '-json' after the tx hex, throwing 'unknown command' — fixed by having CommandLineRawTx use gArgs.GetCommand().

result.card: This PR makes bitcoind's command-line tools (bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-tx, bitcoin-wallet) parse options GNU/getopt-long style, allowing options like -rpcwallet or -wallet to appear after the command rather than being silently swallowed as positional arguments. The core change lives in ArgsManager (utils) with direct effects on bitcoin-cli (rpc) and bitcoin-tx (tools); a release note is the only docs artifact. The strongest evidence of importance is the PR's own before/after transcripts showing that a misplaced -rpcwallet option previously caused an RPC command to silently target the wrong wallet, and unrecognized options after a command are now hard errors instead of silent no-ops. Reviewer w0xlt did substantive, multi-round review, surfaced several real edge-case regressions (a '--' scope bug, a Windows path-vs-option ambiguity, a lone-dash misparse, and a bitcoin-tx regression breaking trailing -json), all of which were fixed in the final push, and then ACKed that exact commit. Reviewer vicjuma raised a scope-consistency question about other tools but deferred rather than objecting; the author explained the narrower scope with follow-up work planned. This PR was extracted from the larger, now-closed #33540.
